dish.title: Jamaican Escovitch Fish: Pan-Fried Snapper with Pickled Pepper-Onion Escovitch and Rice
dish.description: Skin-on red snapper fillets rubbed with lime, dredged in seasoned flour, and pan-fried until golden, then topped with a hot, tangy escovitch of onion, carrot, red bell pepper, garlic, and Scotch bonnet quick-cooked in vinegar with allspice and thyme. Served with steamed white rice.

recipe_version.title: Jamaican Escovitch Fish: Pan-Fried Snapper with Pickled Pepper-Onion Escovitch and Rice
recipe_version.description: Skin-on red snapper fillets rubbed with lime, dredged in seasoned flour, and pan-fried until golden, then topped with a hot, tangy escovitch of onion, carrot, red bell pepper, garlic, and Scotch bonnet quick-cooked in vinegar with allspice and thyme. Served with steamed white rice.

ingredients.name: skin-on red snapper
ingredients.display_name: skin-on red snapper portions, about 6 oz each

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp fish, 1/2 tsp escovitch, 1/2 tsp rice

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Rinse the rice. Slice the onion, julienne the carrot, cut the pepper into strips, and slice the garlic. Wearing gloves, seed and slice the Scotch bonnet. Pat the fish dry, rub with the lime juice, and season with 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Put the flour in a shallow dish.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.body: Combine the rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and 1/2 tsp salt in a 2-quart saucepan. Bring to a boil over high, about 4 minutes, then cover, turn to low, and cook 15 minutes; leave it covered off the heat to rest 10 minutes. The covered cooking and rest run inside steps 3 to 5 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Make the escovitch
steps.body: In a 3-quart saucepan bring the vinegar, 1/4 cup water, sugar, allspice, thyme, and 1/2 tsp salt to a boil over high, about 3 minutes. Add the onion, carrot, pepper, Scotch bonnet, and garlic and simmer 2 minutes, until crisp-tender. Take off the heat.

steps.title: Pan-fry the fish
steps.body: Heat the 1/2 cup oil in a 12-inch skillet (a thin layer, about 1/8 inch) over medium-high until shimmering, about 3 minutes. Dredge 2 fillets in flour, shake off the excess, and lay them in skin side down. Pan-fry until golden and crisp, about 4 minutes, flip, and cook until the fish flakes and reaches 145 F, 2 to 3 minutes. Drain on a rack and repeat with the other 2 fillets (2 batches).

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Plate the rice and fish and spoon the hot escovitch vegetables and some of the pickling liquid over the fish.

coverage_contribution: An HH001 fish dinner with a pickled-vegetable topping, a flavor the catalog's fish meals lack. Jamaica is new as a label (live Caribbean meals are jerk pork chops and grilled mahi-mahi).
near_duplicate_review: Compared with senegalese-fish-yassa: a sharp vinegar pickle with Scotch bonnet and allspice, not slow-cooked lemon-mustard onions. Compared with red-snapper-veracruzana: pan-fried fillets under a pickled vegetable escovitch, not fish braised in tomato-olive sauce. Compared with pan-fried-trout-lemon-capers: a hot vinegar pickle over the fish, not a lemon-caper butter. Compared with jamaican-jerk-pork-chops: fish, and no jerk marinade.
not_duplicate_of: Fillets, not whole fried fish, to keep it weeknight-friendly.
